title: braunrate scenario
description: The scenario file format. The editor uses this file to complete keys and point at errors before you run.

name.description: The scenario name. It appears at the top of the report.

target.description: Base address of the service under test. Example: http://127.0.0.1:8080. Use ${VARIABLE} so a real host does not get versioned.

requires.description: External infrastructure without which this scenario does not run. The CI example loop skips it with a warning instead of breaking.

variables.description: Values reused across the scenario. ${NAME:-default} reads from an environment variable with a fallback.

auth.description: How the credential is obtained, once, before the load starts, and how it is sent on every step.

tls.description: TLS to reach an HTTPS target: a private CA when the certificate is not signed by one the machine already trusts, and a client certificate when the target asks for mTLS.

messaging.description: How to reach Kafka and RabbitMQ when the broker asks for a credential. The default is still a local broker with no authentication.

kafka.description: The Kafka cluster the kafka and await steps talk to.

amqp.description: The RabbitMQ server the amqp and await steps talk to.

data.description: Data sources. Each key becomes a prefix usable as ${name.column}.

scenario.description: Steps run in order, from the first to the last, once per scheduled arrival.

slo.description: The rules that decide whether the run passed. A failing rule makes the command exit with code 1.

load.description: How the load is applied. The default is the open model: the rate does not depend on the target answering.

model.description: 'open' (the default) declares an arrival rate. 'closed' declares users in a loop: the rate becomes a consequence of the response time, and the report says a freeze in the target does not show up in the numbers.

profiles.description: Stretches run in sequence. Open model only.

users.description: Number of simultaneous loops. Closed model only.

duration.description: How long the users stay in the loop. Closed model only.

thinkTime.description: How long each user waits between one iteration and the next. Closed model only.

model.description: 'open' (the default) declares an arrival rate. 'closed' declares users in a loop.

ramp.description: The rate rises linearly from one value to another.

from.description: The rate at the start of the stretch.

to.description: The rate at the end of the stretch.

steady.description: A constant rate for the declared time.

rate.description: The rate held for the whole stretch.

spike.description: An instant jump to the declared rate.

step.description: One step of the scenario. The short form fits on one line: 'http: GET /orders/1'.

name.description: The step name in the report and in the SLO rules. With no name, the protocol aggregation key is used.

weight.description: The share of this alternative in the mix. Each iteration runs one alternative. Either every step declares a weight or none does, and a weight does not coexist with a chained capture.

http.description: The short form ('GET /path') or an object with method, path, headers, body and timeout.

capture.description: Keeps a value from the response for the steps that follow. One line per value: 'invoiceId: $.lastInvoice.id'.

oneOf.description: A JSON path, a header, a cookie or a regular expression.

expect.description: What has to hold for the step to count as a success. Without it, only a network failure or a timeout counts as an error.

graphql.description: A GraphQL operation. The query can come on its own (the operation name is read from it) or inside a map with variables.

kafka.description: Produces a message on the topic. The key decides the partition, so it has to vary per iteration.

amqp.description: Publishes a message to a queue or an exchange.

await.description: Waits for this iteration's message to show up at the destination, closing the measurement of the asynchronous chain.

mqtt.description: Publishes a message to an MQTT topic.

path.description: The path, appended to the target. ${} references make every request different from the last.

headers.description: Headers of this step. The credential header is injected by the auth block and does not need to be repeated here.

body.description: An object becomes JSON. Text goes as it is.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the response before counting the request as a timeout.

followRedirects.description: Whether to follow 3xx. Following changes what is measured: the number becomes the sum of the hops.

detailedCapture.description: The long form of a capture, for when a default value is needed or the capture may fail on purpose.

from.description: Where the value comes from in the response: a JSONPath, a header, or a regular expression.

default.description: The value used when the capture finds nothing.

required.description: True by default. A required capture that fails ends the iteration with a correlation error.

expect.description: What has to be true about the response. A failure here counts as an error in the report.

status.description: The status that counts as a success. One number: a step that accepts more than one status is two steps.

json.description: The expected JSON path. Example: '$.status: PAID'. Use 'exists' to only check presence.

header.description: A header that has to come back, with the value it has to have.

bodyContains.description: Text that has to appear in the response body.

auth.description: How the engine obtains a credential and injects it into every step. The step does not have to declare a header.

type.description: token obtains a credential and sends it on every step; basic sends user and password; header sends a fixed line, for an API key already in the environment.

obtain.description: The login request, performed once for the whole run. See ADR 0005.

http.description: The login request. Only the environment and fixed values fit here: the login happens before the journeys, so a value captured by a step does not exist yet.

capture.description: What is taken from the login response. The name declared here is what ${token} refers to.

refreshAfter.description: How long before the credential is obtained again. Without it, the same credential lasts the whole run.

header.description: The whole header line, name and value.

password.description: The password, for type: basic. Only the name of an environment variable: a literal value fails validation.

dataSource.description: A CSV file or synthetic generation. Without it every iteration uses the same value and the target answers from cache.

file.description: A CSV file, read relative to the scenario. The header line names the columns, and each one becomes ${source.column}.

consume.description: circular loops from the start to the end of the file; uniquePerUser never repeats a value.

seed.description: Same seed, same data. It takes ${SEED:-42} to come from the environment. The seed that ran and the variable it came from go into the report and into the JSON.

generate.description: Synthetic fields. One value per iteration, stable across the whole journey.

sloRule.description: One rule per step, or for 'global', 'journey' and 'regression'. Example: '- journey: { p95: < 2s }'.

p50.description: The limit for half of the requests of this step.

p75.description: The limit for 75% of the requests of this step.

p90.description: The limit for 90% of the requests of this step.

p95.description: The limit for 95% of the requests of this step.

p99.description: The limit for 99% of the requests of this step.

p99.9.description: The limit for 99.9% of the requests of this step.

max.description: The limit for the worst request of this step.

errors.description: A percentage. '< 0.1' is one tenth of one percent.

success.description: A percentage. '>= 99.9' is the mirror reading of 'errors: < 0.1'.

throughput.description: 'global' only. Completed requests per second. Example: '>= 200/s'.

journeyP50.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

journeyP75.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

journeyP90.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

journeyP95.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

journeyP99.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

journeyP99.9.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

journeyMax.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

globalP50.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

globalP75.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

globalP90.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

globalP95.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

globalP99.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

globalP99.9.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

globalMax.description: 'regression' only. How much worse it may get against the baseline. Example: '<= 10%% worse'.

limit.description: A comparison with a unit. Examples: '< 150ms', '>= 250/s', '< 0.1'.

examples: query LookUpOrder($id: ID!) { order(id: $id) { id status } }

operation.description: The operation name. Only needed when the query carries more than one.

variables.description: The operation variables. It takes ${data.column} and captured values.

path.description: The GraphQL endpoint. The default fits almost every service.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the response before counting the request as a timeout.

topic.description: The topic the message is produced to. It is also the name the report aggregates the step under.

key.description: The message key. An always-identical key sends everything to the same partition, and the number comes out optimistic.

value.description: An object becomes JSON; text goes as it is.

acks.description: How many replicas acknowledge before the message counts as delivered.

partition.description: Sends every message of this step to a single partition, ignoring the key. It concentrates the load on purpose, and the report says the number belongs to one partition.

group.description: The consumer group to watch during the run. The report shows how many messages it fell behind, read from the broker.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the confirmation before counting the produce as a timeout.

queue.description: The common case: publishes straight to the queue, which is declared if it does not exist.

exchange.description: The exchange the message is published to. Without it, the message goes to the default exchange and 'queue' is the routing key.

routingKey.description: The routing key, when an exchange is declared.

body.description: The message body. An object comes out as JSON.

messageId.description: Goes out as message-id and works as the correlation for the await step.

url.description: The RabbitMQ server. With a credential in it, declare the whole URL through an environment variable.

persistent.description: Whether the broker writes the message to disk before confirming.

confirm.description: Waits for the broker to confirm. Turning it off measures the write to the socket, not the delivery.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the confirmation before counting the publish as a timeout.

topic.description: The topic where the effect shows up.

brokers.description: The cluster, when it is not the one in the messaging block.

kafka.description: The topic where the effect shows up.

queue.description: The queue where the effect shows up.

topic.description: The topic where the effect shows up.

url.description: The server, when it is not the one in the messaging block.

amqp.description: The queue where the effect shows up.

http.description: Polls a request until the 'until' condition holds. For a system that only shows the effect through an API.

path.description: The path polled until the condition in 'to' holds.

key.description: The value that identifies this iteration's message.

field.description: A JSON path inside the message, when the correlation is not in the key.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the effect before counting the step as a timeout.

interval.description: How often to poll. The measured latency has that granularity.

until.description: The condition that ends the wait over http: status, bodyContains or a JSON path with the expected value.

generatedField.description: A short recipe ("uuid", "number(10,500)") or the long form with type, format and newEvery.

type.description: The generator. pattern builds a value in the shape declared in 'format'; cpf and cnpj come out with a valid check digit.

format.description: For type: pattern only. # becomes a digit, @ becomes a letter, everything else comes out literal.

newEvery.description: iteration keeps the same value across the whole journey, which is what an idempotency key needs.

broker.description: How to reach the broker. A secret never stays in the file: 'password' only takes a reference to an environment variable, like ${KAFKA_PASSWORD}.

type.description: saslPlain and scramSha* use a user and a password. mskIam signs with the standard AWS chain and never asks for a key. certificate is mTLS. OAUTHBEARER is not in v1.

user.description: The broker user. It can come from ${VARIABLE}.

password.description: A reference to an environment variable only: ${KAFKA_PASSWORD}. A literal value is refused at validation, and so is a fallback value, because the fallback would be the secret written in the file.

region.description: The AWS region, required for mskIam.

auth.description: How the broker authenticates. A literal password fails validation: only the name of an environment variable, or the standard cloud chain.

tls.description: TLS to reach the broker. true uses the system authorities; the object form declares a private CA or a client certificate.

key.description: The key of the client certificate.

tls.description: true for TLS with the system CAs, or a map with a private CA and a client certificate.

topic.description: The topic the message is published to.

payload.description: The message payload. An object comes out as JSON.

qos.description: Delivery guarantee: 0 fire-and-forget, 1 at-least-once (waits for the broker's acknowledgement), 2 exactly-once.

retain.description: Whether the broker keeps the message as the topic's last known value for future subscribers.

broker.description: The MQTT broker, when it is not the scenario target. tcp:// for plain, ssl:// for TLS.

clientId.description: The client id the broker sees. Defaults to a single stable id for the run.

username.description: Username, when the broker asks for one.

password.description: Password, declared through an environment variable.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the connection and the acknowledgement before counting a timeout.
